action: Test one append-only-looking GitHub issue-event identity surface as a zero-cost Chat-visible witness external to rewindable Git refs, explicitly falsifying editable content, deletion/recreation and monotonicity assumptions before promotion.

positive: Issue-event objects are external to Git branch/ref state, so same-repository force-ref rewind does not itself rewind a pinned event object.
GitHub documents each issue event with a unique integer id, Global Node ID and created_at; the public REST issue-event surface exposes list/get operations rather than event mutation operations.
Issue deletion can surface as 410 Gone to an authorized reader, so a verifier that rejects missing witness state can fail closed rather than silently accept a missing event.
negative: Issue title/body and comments are not append-only: they are editable, comments are deletable, and issue-description edit history can be removed. They are rejected as monotonic witnesses.
The issue that owns the event stream can be permanently deleted by authorized administrators/owners.

The reviewed current GitHub docs do not state that issue-event ids/node_ids or issue numbers are never reused after deletion/recreation, and they do not state a monotonic ordering/counter guarantee for repository issue events.
There is no direct create-issue-event primitive; a fresh event requires an auxiliary issue/pull-request activity mutation.
result.anti_aba_consequence: A pinned event identity is useful as a fail-closed external tamper sentinel, but a unique external object is not automatically a monotonic witness. Without a documented non-reuse/ordering property and a dedicated append step, this leaf does not close same-repository force-ref ABA from r202/r203.

Do not promote it to the required non-rewindable monotonic anti-ABA anchor unless a later leaf establishes a repository-scoped monotonic/no-reuse allocator or equivalent externally queryable head semantics.
